market_question: Will the US acquire part of Greenland in 2026?
reasoning: Despite Trump's renewed interest, Greenland’s leadership and Denmark have firmly rejected any sale or transfer of territory. Any binding agreement—whether a purchase, long-term lease, or treaty granting exclusive jurisdiction—would face insurmountable political, legislative, and diplomatic hurdles within 2026. The 14.5% market probability overestimates the likelihood of a rapid, substantial shift in sovereignty.
evidence_points: Greenland's Prime Minister has repeatedly stated the island is not for sale.
Danish government supports Greenland's self-determination and opposes cession.
No serious negotiations, legislative drafts, or binding instruments have surfaced as of early 2026.
Historical precedent: past US attempts to buy Greenland (1946, 2019) were rejected quickly.
sources_consulted: Reuters / AP coverage on US-Greenland relations
